title: Interlock sprint calendar and capacity guardrails for multi-surface launches
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a single interlock sprint calendar and a set of enforceable capacity guardrails to coordinate a multi-surface (runtime, console, API) launch across regions. This ticket captures the cross-team schedule, gating matrix, capacity reservation requirements, canary choreography, rollback windows, and runbook ownership. The calendar must minimize blast radius while maximizing predictability for customers and sales. Key constraints: Dedicated capacity procurement lead times, regional compliance windows, and console UI dependencies that cannot ship before API contracts are stable.
milestones: Draft interlock calendar and gating matrix (PM + Eng + Design) - due 2025-02-18
Confirm Dedicated capacity reservation and autoscale policies with Infra - due 2025-02-21
Finalize canary choreography and monitoring hooks (runtime + console + api) - due 2025-02-25
Publish cutover checklist and runbook, including rollback triggers - due 2025-03-04
Execute staged canary in us-west (small traffic) - target 2025-03-10
Regional ramp to EU + APAC, staggered windows per legal/regional constraints - target 2025-03-14
acceptance_criteria: Calendar ratified by PM leads, Eng leads (runtime/console/api), and Design - signoffs recorded
Capacity reservations confirmed with billing and infra (PO/commit ID recorded)
Automated rollout policy deployed to Console with canary cohorts and rollback thresholds configured
End-to-end smoke tests covering runtime -> API -> Console paths pass in canary cluster
Runbook published with clear owners, pager rotations, and escalation matrix
risks: Dedicated capacity procurement delays could push the canary window beyond target dates
Console feature depends on API contract change; mismatch could force console rollback while runtime continues
Regional compliance holds (data residency) may require duplicated staging environments and extra lead time
If KV cache warm-up is slower than expected for canary traffic, latency SLOs may be violated and trigger rollback
Monitoring gaps for cross-surface traces could lengthen mean time to detect (MTTD) issues during rollout
